content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an audio-video transformer, AVT, which uses an audio-video contrastive loss function, audio-video matching loss, and *a novel masked audio model* to achieve competitive results on VGG-Sound, Kinetics-Sound, and EP-Kitchens. The proposal of masked audio and video learning is interesting but needs more experiments to verify its effectiveness compared to VideoMAE.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[Strength]
1. The proposed masked audio-video reconstruction loss L_{MASegmV} uses some statistics to detect salient activity segments and then apply masks and reconstruction. This may help to learn useful features with less computation.

[Weakness]
1. The definition of different losses is unclear. In the audio-video contrastive loss L_{AVC}, `A and V are from the same sample or not` computed at batch-level or instance level? If it's batch-level, what's the difference between L_{AVC} and L_{AVM} (Eqn. 2 and Eqn. 4)?

2. Following 1., I assume the granularity of AV is captured by Eqn. (5) (which is also experimentally verified in Table 4), but it seems there is a lack of results showing how good  L_{MASegmV} itself achieves. How did it compare to L_{MAV} (i.e. VideoMAE) only? 

3. In Table 3, SOTA results on Epic-Kitchens-100 are outdated, please refer to paper-with-code for details.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: There are too many losses (4 losses) involved and usually, one of them dominates. It looks that the standard CE loss L_{AVC} dominates and thus makes this work less exciting. L_{AVC} and L_{AVM} look unclear to me and have also been extensively studied by previous work. The self-supervised loss, L_{MASegmV} looks quite interesting but lacks of specific experimental results to verify its effectiveness.
content.summary_of_the_review: An interesting combination of different losses for audio-video feature learning but lacks a specific analysis of the new loss, i.e L_{MASegmV}.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an audio-video fusion transformer for the task of action recognition. Instead of concatenating or exchanging query/key matrices like previous works, the proposed method proposes an AVBottleneck block, which uses a set of learnable tokens to fuse the audio and video features. The computational complexity will be reduced if the number of learnable tokens is smaller than the number of video/audio tokens. The authors further add reconstruction loss and contrastive loss to enhance the performance. The authors show that the proposed audio-video fusion transformer can achieve better performance on several public datasets while being computationally efficient.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
In my opinion, the strengths of this paper are as follows:
1. The paper is well-written and easy to understand. Enough information is provided to reproduce the proposed method in this paper.
2. The proposed AVBottleneck block is interesting. Compared with MBT, it is a new method that can efficiently fuse multimodal features without increasing too much computational complexity. 
3. The experimental result of the full method is strong on 2 of the 3 public datasets. 

Here are the weaknesses of this paper:
1. Better ablation study could be conducted to see the usefulness of the proposed AVBottleneck. In the ablation study, I see great performance improvement after adding the contrastive loss and mask reconstruction losses. In my opinion, adding these losses is not the major contribution of this work. To better show the performance improvement of AVBottleneck, I suggest two experiments, one is to directly compare AVBottleneck with MBT bottleneck (both without other losses). The other is to add the AVC, AVM, and MASegmV without the AVBottleneck.
2. With all the techniques used, the performance improvement is only marginal. The only large improvement is achieved on the Kinetics-Sounds dataset, however, in Table 4, the Video Only (16 f) result is already much better than all previous methods, I also hope to see the explanation from the authors on this part.
3. It could be better if the authors can analyze the choice of L in the experiment.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper is clear enough in representation and has reasonable quality.

I believe the paper contains enough information to reproduce, but I am not 100% certain. 

There is novelty in this work but not so much, since the AVBottleneck can be seen as an improvement of MBT, and MASegm is a small variation of random audio masking, while contrastive loss and masked video and audio losses are widely adopted techniques.
content.summary_of_the_review:
I think this paper proposes an interesting AVBottleneck block for efficiently fusing multimodal inputs. However, the performance improvement and technical novelty are limited while more experiments are needed to holistically see the usefulness of the AVBottleneck block.

I am willing to change my rating based on the authors' feedback.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This manuscript studies the multimodal action recognition, specifically on how to better fuse the video-audio signals during the training. Inspired by prior work MBT [1], the manuscript proposed to process the video and audio embeddings by the bottleneck transformer. A few auxiliary losses are prosed and used to facilitate the cross-modal learning, including the cross-modal contrastive loss, structured masked audio modeling loss and audio-video matching loss. Experiments are conducted on three public benchmarks and two in-house datasets, showing the state-of-the-art performance on audio-visual action recognition results. 

[1] Nagrani, A., Yang, S., Arnab, A., Jansen, A., Schmid, C. and Sun, C., 2021. Attention bottlenecks for multimodal fusion. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 34, pp.14200-14213.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strength
* The manuscript is composed logically clean and written smoothly. The reviewer could easily follow their proposals and ideas. 
* The structured masked modeling on audio is an interesting idea and the improvement is  (~0.5 top1) according to the ablations.

# Weakness
* The reviewer thinks most of the components of this framework are existing and well-presented in the fields. For example the model architecture is borrowed from MBT[1] and the auxiliary losses (contrastive loss, masked modeling loss and matching loss) are commonly used in self-supervised learning.
* The ablations on different losses and experiment set-ups lack discussion.
* Could we add one more column about training epochs when comparing different methods? it seems that the training epochs are quite different across methods, e.g. AVT trains for 100 epochs while MBT trains for 50 epochs.
* Some references may not be correct. For example, In the paper, the author mentioned "Computational complexity. The multimodal bottleneck Transformer reduces the computing complexity ... merged concatenation based multimodal attention (Akbari et al., 2021)." From VATT (Akbari et al., 2021), is there any concatenation operation for fusing multimodal representation?
* Visualization could be improved. Fig.2 and Fig.4 are too dense and each figure is too small to read.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
* Clarity and quality: The manuscript is cleanly written with good quality. The reviewer could easily follow their proposals and ideas. 
* Novelty: Most of the methodology, model architectures and losses exist and are well-known in the community. For example, the model architecture is originated from MBT[1], with the visual backbone replaced by the state-of-the-art video model. The cross-model contrastive loss, the masked modeling and the matching loss are widely used in multimodal self-supervised learning and proven their effectiveness in prior works [2, 3, 4]. This work effectively combines them and shows the improvements on audio-visual action recognition task. One idea that might be more interesting described in this paper is the structured masking strategy on audio, where the spectrums are preprocessed and segmented into semantic chunks and the masking and reconstructing is happening on the semantic chunks instead of on random audio chunks.
* Reproducibility: The reviewer is not clear about the reproducibility of this work since no code is open-sourced yet. Some implementation details are described in the paper.

[1] Nagrani, A., Yang, S., Arnab, A., Jansen, A., Schmid, C. and Sun, C., 2021. Attention bottlenecks for multimodal fusion. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 34, pp.14200-14213.
[2] Akbari, H., Yuan, L., Qian, R., Chuang, W.H., Chang, S.F., Cui, Y. and Gong, B., 2021. Vatt: Transformers for multimodal self-supervised learning from raw video, audio and text. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 34, pp.24206-24221.
[3] Xu, H., Ghosh, G., Huang, P.Y., Okhonko, D., Aghajanyan, A., Metze, F., Zettlemoyer, L. and Feichtenhofer, C., 2021. Videoclip: Contrastive pre-training for zero-shot video-text understanding. arXiv preprint arXiv:2109.14084.
[4] Li, D., Li, J., Li, H., Niebles, J.C. and Hoi, S.C., 2022. Align and Prompt: Video-and-Language Pre-training with Entity Prompts. In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (pp. 4953-4963).
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall the reviewer thinks the manuscript is a good application paper and the improvement on audio-visual action recognition task is significant. However, the methodology and novelty could be improved as most of them exist.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposed a multi-modal transformer to improve action recognition accuracy, named Audio-Video Transformer (AVT). It has five contributions and designs: (1) Use a combination of audio and visual signals as input, no just visual signals. (2) Use an audio-video contrastive loss to penalizes the distribution divergence of audio and video representations for the same sample. (3) Propose the AVBottleneck structure based on [1] to decrease the computational complexity. (4) Design an audio-video matching loss to forces the multimodal Transformer to learn high level semantic labels precisely. (5) Design a masked audio-video loss, which mask a proportion of the audio activity segments, instead of directly mask audio signal randomly. Then, this paper shows exhaustive experimental results in 5 datasets (3 public datasets and 2 in-house datasets) . 

Reference:

[1] Arsha Nagrani, Shan Yang, Anurag Arnab, Aren Jansen, Cordelia Schmid, and Chen Sun. Attention bottlenecks for multimodal fusion. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 34, 2021.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 

+ Selected mask strategy (instead of random mask) is an interesting insight.
+ Experiments are exhaustive and results in Kinetics-Sounds dataset are excellent (8% accuracy improvement).  

Weakness: 

- This paper claims that they develop the first Audio-Video Transformer, but some papers have proposed or applied audio-visual transformer architecture [2] [3] [4]. 
- Some contributions are just the application of existing methods (contrastive loss, bottleneck fusion).
- Experiment results in VGGSound dataset is not good.
- Ablation study shows the effect of some proposed methods are limited (e.g. The audio-visual matching loss is almost useless in Kinetics-Sounds and Epic-Kitchens-100 datasets.).
- Why just mask audio segments in the train stage?  Lack of ablation study or explanation of masking visual segments.

Reference :

[2] Thanh-Dat Truong, Chi Nhan Duong, The De Vu, Hoang Anh Pham, Bhiksha Raj, Ngan Le, Khoa Luu. The Right To Talk: An Audio-Visual Transformer Approach. Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), pp. 1105-1114, 2021.
[3] Yan-Bo Lin, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang. Audiovisual Transformer with Instance Attention for Audio-Visual Event Localization. Proceedings of the Asian Conference on Computer Vision (ACCV), 2020.
[4] Wim Boes, Hugo Van hamme. Audiovisual Transformer Architectures for Large-Scale Classification and Synchronization of Weakly Labeled Audio Events. Proceedings of the 27th ACM International Conference on Multimedia. pp. 1961-1969, 2019.

content.title: AVT: Audio-Video Transformer for Multimodal Action Recognition
content.abstract: Action recognition is an essential field for video understanding. To learn from heterogeneous data sources effectively, in this work, we propose a novel multimodal action recognition approach termed Audio-Video Transformer (AVT). AVT uses a combination of video and audio signals to improve action recognition accuracy, leveraging the effective spatio-temporal representation by the video Transformer. For multimodal fusion, simply concatenating multimodal tokens in a cross-modal Transformer requires large computational and memory resources, instead we reduce the cross-modality complexity through an audio-video bottleneck Transformer. To improve the learning efficiency of multimodal Transformer, we integrate self-supervised objectives, i.e., audio-video contrastive learning, audio-video matching, and masked audio and video learning, into AVT training, which maps diverse audio and video representations into a common multimodal representation space. We further propose a masked audio segment loss to learn semantic audio activities in AVT. Extensive experiments and ablation studies on three public datasets and two in-house datasets consistently demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed AVT. Specifically, AVT outperforms its previous state-of-the-art counterparts on Kinetics-Sounds and Epic-Kitchens-100 datasets by 8% and 1%, respectively, without external training data. AVT also surpasses one of the previous state-of-the-art video Transformers by 10% on the VGGSound dataset by leveraging the audio signal. Compared to one of the previous state-of-the-art multimodal Transformers, AVT is 1.3x more efficient in terms of FLOPs and improves the accuracy by 4.2% on Epic-Kitchens-100. Visualization results further demonstrate that the audio provides complementary and discriminative features, and our AVT can effectively understand the action from a combination of audio and video.
